checks.question: Are there nested loops, repeated scans, brute-force matching, or quadratic behavior over potentially large inputs (algorithmic complexity unsuitable for input size)? (PER-001)

onYes.title: Fix algorithmic complexity (PER-001): use better algorithms/data structures
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Super-linear algorithms over large inputs cause severe slowdowns and timeouts.

Find all instances: Search for nested loops, repeated scans, and brute-force matching over collections that can grow large.

Fix correctly: Use better algorithms, maps/sets for lookups, indexes, batching, or precomputation to reduce complexity.

Constraints: Preserve correctness; verify results match. Measure before/after where feasible.

Acceptance: Hot paths scale acceptably with input size. Add a test/benchmark or complexity check for large inputs.

checks.question: Are there loops issuing one database query per item or per relation (N+1 database query)? (PER-002)

onYes.title: Fix N+1 query (PER-002): batch, join, or eager-load
onYes.prompt:
Problem: N+1 queries multiply DB round trips and dominate latency.

Find all instances: Search for loops that query the DB per element or per related entity.

Fix correctly: Batch, join, prefetch/eager-load, or use set-based queries to fetch in bulk.

Constraints: Avoid over-fetching (PER-004). Preserve result correctness.

Acceptance: Per-item DB fan-out is eliminated. Add a test/check asserting a bounded query count for N items.

checks.question: Do hot-path database queries filter/sort on unindexed or low-selectivity fields (query not aligned with index/selectivity)? (PER-003)

onYes.title: Fix unindexed queries (PER-003): align predicates with indexes
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Queries that can't use an index scan large amounts of data, slowing hot paths.

Find all instances: Search hot-path queries filtering/sorting on unindexed or low-selectivity columns.

Fix correctly: Add appropriate indexes or rewrite the query/predicate to use existing indexes; verify with the query plan.

Constraints: Weigh index write/storage cost. Keep migrations safe (OPS-013/OPS-015).

Acceptance: Hot queries use indexes. Add a migration/index and verify the plan; keep tests passing.

checks.question: Do queries retrieve full rows, large blobs, or unbounded result sets when only small fields are needed (over-fetching rows/columns)? (PER-004)

onYes.title: Fix over-fetching (PER-004): select only needed fields and limit rows
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Over-fetching wastes bandwidth, memory, and time.

Find all instances: Search for SELECT * / full-entity loads / unbounded result sets where only a few fields/rows are needed.

Fix correctly: Select only required columns, apply limits/pagination, and avoid loading large blobs unnecessarily.

Constraints: Keep correctness; don't drop fields the caller needs. Use stable pagination (PER-017).

Acceptance: Queries fetch only what's needed. Add a test/check asserting bounded result size.

checks.question: Are large collections loaded into memory then filtered, grouped, joined, or sorted locally (large in-memory sort/filter)? (PER-005)

onYes.title: Fix in-memory sort/filter (PER-005): push down to storage or stream
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Loading everything then filtering in memory wastes memory and time.

Find all instances: Search for fetch-all-then-filter/sort/group/join in application code.

Fix correctly: Push filtering/sorting/aggregation to the database/storage, or process as a stream.

Constraints: Preserve result correctness/ordering (use stable order, DAT-013).

Acceptance: Filtering/sorting happens at the source or via streaming. Add a test/check confirming the data isn't fully materialized.

checks.question: Are expensive deterministic computations repeated in loops, hot paths, or request handlers (recomputing expensive pure result)? (PER-006)

onYes.title: Fix recomputation (PER-006): memoize/precompute with invalidation
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Recomputing the same expensive pure result wastes CPU.

Find all instances: Search for repeated expensive deterministic computations in loops/hot paths.

Fix correctly: Memoize, cache, or precompute the result and hoist it out of loops, with correct invalidation if inputs change.

Constraints: Bound cache size/TTL (RES-005). Ensure invalidation correctness (PER-015).

Acceptance: Expensive pure results are computed once. Add a test/benchmark confirming reduced recomputation.

checks.question: Are independent API/database/RPC calls performed sequentially despite no data dependency (serial independent external calls)? (PER-007)

onYes.title: Fix serial independent calls (PER-007): parallelize under bounded concurrency
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Running independent calls serially adds up their latencies needlessly.

Find all instances: Search for sequential independent external calls with no data dependency.

Fix correctly: Batch or run them in parallel under bounded concurrency; await all and handle partial failures.

Constraints: Bound concurrency to avoid overload (ERR-010). Handle individual failures (ERR-011).

Acceptance: Independent calls run concurrently. Add a test/check confirming parallel execution and correct aggregation.

checks.question: Are hot locks protecting large critical sections or unrelated shared state, causing excessive lock contention? (PER-008)

onYes.title: Fix lock contention (PER-008): shrink critical sections or shard state
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Coarse hot locks serialize work and limit throughput.

Find all instances: Search for hot locks guarding large sections or unrelated state.

Fix correctly: Reduce critical-section size, shard/partition state, use lock-free/concurrent structures, or isolate ownership.

Constraints: Preserve correctness/invariants; avoid introducing races (CON-001).

Acceptance: Lock contention is reduced. Add a benchmark/check or review confirming smaller/partitioned critical sections.

checks.question: Are there frequent polling loops checking external state or database rows (inefficient polling)? (PER-009)

onYes.title: Fix inefficient polling (PER-009): use events or bounded backoff
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Tight polling wastes CPU/DB/network and adds latency.

Find all instances: Search for frequent polling of external state or DB rows.

Fix correctly: Use events/subscriptions/notifications where available, or bounded backoff with jitter when polling is unavoidable.

Constraints: Config over hardcoding for intervals. Avoid busy-wait (CON-020).

Acceptance: Polling is event-driven or backed off. Add a test/check asserting the reduced polling frequency.

checks.question: Do workflows require many small network round trips for one user-visible operation (chatty network protocol)? (PER-010)

onYes.title: Fix chatty protocol (PER-010): batch, coarsen, pipeline, or cache
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Many small round trips per operation add latency and overhead.

Find all instances: Search for operations that make many small sequential network calls.

Fix correctly: Batch requests, coarsen the API, pipeline, or cache to reduce round trips.

Constraints: Preserve correctness; bound batch sizes.

Acceptance: Round trips per operation are reduced. Add a test/check asserting fewer calls per operation.

checks.question: Is there repeated large object/buffer/string/array/collection allocation in hot paths (large allocation in hot path)? (PER-011)

onYes.title: Fix hot-path allocation (PER-011): reuse buffers or reduce allocation
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Frequent large allocations in hot paths cause GC pressure and latency spikes.

Find all instances: Search hot paths for repeated large allocations (buffers, strings, arrays, collections).

Fix correctly: Reuse buffers/pools, stream data, reduce allocation size, or hoist allocation out of the hot path.

Constraints: Preserve correctness and thread-safety of any reused buffers (CON-009).

Acceptance: Hot-path allocations are reduced. Add a benchmark/check confirming lower allocation.

checks.question: Is there repeated concatenation, slicing, encoding, decoding, cloning, or serialization in loops (excessive string/data copying)? (PER-012)

onYes.title: Fix excessive copying (PER-012): use builders/buffers/views
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Repeated copying/encoding in loops wastes CPU and memory.

Find all instances: Search loops for repeated string concatenation, slicing, encode/decode, clone, or serialize operations.

Fix correctly: Use builders/buffers, views/slices, streaming encoders, or fewer transformations.

Constraints: Preserve output correctness.

Acceptance: Redundant copying is reduced. Add a benchmark/check or review confirming the improvement.

checks.question: Are complex regexes run on untrusted or long input that may backtrack exponentially (catastrophic regex backtracking)? (PER-013)

onYes.title: Fix catastrophic backtracking (PER-013): simplify regex or bound input
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Pathological regexes (nested quantifiers) can hang on crafted input (ReDoS).

Find all instances: Search for complex regexes (nested/ambiguous quantifiers) applied to untrusted or long input.

Fix correctly: Simplify the regex to avoid ambiguity, use a linear-time regex engine, bound input length, and apply a match timeout.

Constraints: Preserve matching semantics for valid input. Combine with regex-injection (INJ-008).

Acceptance: Regexes can't be DoS'd. Add a test with a backtracking payload asserting bounded time/rejection.

checks.question: Do cache misses cause many concurrent workers to recompute or refetch the same expensive value (cache stampede/thundering herd)? (PER-014)

onYes.title: Fix cache stampede (PER-014): coalesce requests and add jitter
onYes.prompt:
Problem: On a cache miss, many workers recompute the same value simultaneously, overloading the source.

Find all instances: Search for cache-miss paths where concurrent callers recompute/refetch the same key.

Fix correctly: Add request coalescing (single-flight), per-key locking, TTL jitter, and stale-while-revalidate.

Constraints: Bound recompute concurrency. Keep correctness of served data.

Acceptance: Concurrent misses don't stampede. Add a concurrency test asserting a single recompute for many simultaneous callers.

checks.question: Are there caches without TTL, versioning, invalidation events, or clear ownership (missing cache invalidation policy)? (PER-015)

onYes.title: Fix missing cache invalidation (PER-015): define TTL and invalidation
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Caches without an invalidation policy serve stale data indefinitely.

Find all instances: Search caches for missing TTL, versioned keys, invalidation triggers, or ownership.

Fix correctly: Define TTL, invalidation triggers on writes, versioned keys, and clear ownership/consistency expectations.

Constraints: Config over hardcoding for TTLs. Invalidate transactionally with source writes (DAT-020).

Acceptance: Caches have a clear invalidation policy. Add a test asserting cached values invalidate on the relevant write.

checks.question: Do caches store sensitive, authorization-dependent, user-specific, or rapidly changing data too broadly or too long (over-caching stale/sensitive data)? (PER-016)

onYes.title: Fix over-caching sensitive data (PER-016): scope keys and shorten TTL
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Caching authorization-dependent or sensitive data too broadly leaks data across users or serves stale/private data.

Find all instances: Search caches for sensitive/user-specific/authorization-dependent or fast-changing data cached broadly or for long TTLs.

Fix correctly: Key caches by authorization/user context, shorten TTLs, or avoid caching unsafe data entirely.

Constraints: Don't cache per-user data under shared keys. Coordinate with privacy (CSP-016/CSP-017).

Acceptance: Caching respects authorization and freshness. Add a test asserting one user can't receive another's cached data.

checks.question: Is offset/limit pagination used over large or frequently changing datasets (offset pagination on large dataset)? (PER-017)

onYes.title: Fix offset pagination (PER-017): use keyset/cursor pagination
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Large offsets are slow (the DB scans/skips many rows) and unstable under concurrent changes.

Find all instances: Search for offset/limit pagination over large/changing datasets.

Fix correctly: Use keyset/cursor pagination with a stable, deterministic ordering.

Constraints: Provide opaque cursors (API-008); keep ordering stable (DAT-013).

Acceptance: Pagination is cursor-based and efficient. Add a test paging deep into a large set asserting stable, fast results.

checks.question: Do startup paths eagerly load large data, initialize unused dependencies, or make slow network calls (slow startup from eager initialization)? (PER-018)

onYes.title: Fix slow startup (PER-018): lazy-load or parallelize initialization
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Heavy eager initialization slows startup and delays readiness/scaling.

Find all instances: Search startup for eager loading of large data, initialization of unused dependencies, and slow network calls.

Fix correctly: Lazy-load on first use, parallelize safe initialization, or move non-essential work out of the startup path.

Constraints: Don't defer required validation (validate config at startup, OPS-009). Avoid config-read-too-early issues (OPS-010).

Acceptance: Startup is faster without losing required checks. Add a test/check confirming deferred/parallel init.

checks.question: Are there high-volume logs inside tight loops, per-item operations, or request hot paths (excessive hot-path logging)? (PER-019)

onYes.title: Fix hot-path logging (PER-019): reduce volume, aggregate, or use metrics
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Logging per item/iteration floods logs and adds latency/I/O.

Find all instances: Search tight loops/per-item/hot paths for verbose logging.

Fix correctly: Lower log volume/level, aggregate or sample, or move counts to metrics instead of per-item logs.

Constraints: Keep essential diagnostics. Avoid high-cardinality labels (OPS-017).

Acceptance: Hot-path logging is bounded. Add a test/check asserting reduced log volume per operation.

checks.question: Are there repeated encode/decode/compress/decompress cycles where data could remain in native or streamed form (unnecessary serialization/compression overhead)? (PER-020)

onYes.title: Fix redundant serialization (PER-020): avoid needless transformations
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Repeated serialize/deserialize/compress/decompress cycles waste CPU.

Find all instances: Search for data repeatedly encoded/decoded/compressed/decompressed where it could stay native or streamed.

Fix correctly: Eliminate redundant transformations; keep data in native/streamed form; compress only when beneficial.

Constraints: Preserve correctness and any required wire formats.

Acceptance: Redundant transformations are removed. Add a benchmark/check confirming fewer encode/decode cycles.
